messages.subject: RunLevelData vs ProcessedData objects after normalization: different results
messages.subject_clean: RunLevelData vs ProcessedData objects after normalization: different results
messages.body_plain:
Dear MSstats dev team,

I am reporting an observation that I just had regarding what seems to be slightly different results between RunLevelData and ProcessedData objects after dataProcess, and ask for your recommendation on which would be the better output to use if one wants to export the summarized+normalized protein abundances from MSstats into an expression matrix in order to continue running the statistics on a different pipeline (i.e. for clustering analysis or multi-variate linear modeling).

Visualization of log2intensities by Protein/Experimental group from the RunLevelData object

normalized_data <- dataProcess(msts_formated_data)

tab_proccessed_data <- normalized_data$RunlevelData

hist(tab_proccessed_data$LogIntensities,
     main = "Normalized Intensities by Protein from 'RunLevelData'")

ggplot(data = tab_proccessed_data,
       aes(x = GROUP_ORIGINAL, y = LogIntensities)) +
   geom_boxplot() +
   ggtitle("Normalized Intensities by Condition from 'RunLevelData'")

It can be noticed an extreme outlier is present

dataProcessPlots(normalized_data,
                 type = "QCplot",
                 which.Protein="allonly",
                 address = FALSE)

The outlier is not noticed when using the function dataProcessPlots

Visualization of log2intensities by Protein/Experimental group from the ProcessedData object

The ProcessedData object was further processed to get the mean Log2 Intensities values per Protein per Run.

tab_proccessed_datatest <- normalized_data$ProcessedData

to_wide <- tab_proccessed_datatest %>%
   select(PROTEIN, ABUNDANCE, GROUP_ORIGINAL, SUBJECT_ORIGINAL) %>%
   mutate(GROUP_REPLICATE_RUN = paste0(GROUP_ORIGINAL,"_",SUBJECT_ORIGINAL)) %>%
   group_by(PROTEIN, GROUP_REPLICATE_RUN) %>%
   summarise(LogIntensities = mean(ABUNDANCE)) %>%
   ungroup() %>%
   separate(col = GROUP_REPLICATE_RUN,
            sep = "\\_",
            into = c("Group", "Replicate_run"))

hist(to_wide$LogIntensities,
     main = "Normalized Intensities by Protein from 'ProcessedData'")

ggplot(data = to_wide,
       aes(x = Group, y = LogIntensities)) +
   geom_boxplot() +
   ggtitle("Normalized Intensities by Condition from 'ProcessedData'")

The outlier is not observed when using the ProcessedData object and further processing to get the mean Log2Intensities of features per Protein per Run.

Is there an explanation for this to happen?

Noticing this, what would make more sense to use if one wants to export a summarized and normalized expression matrix after processing with MSstats? I have been using the RunLevelData object for this purpose but now it seems that there is an outlier filtering step happening before the ProcessedData object is created.

In the same context of this question: is there an argument against using the mean of the log2 intensities of the features per protein per run to get the normalized intensities per protein per run for downstream analysis?

Many thanks as always for taking a look into this and for the MSstats development.

Best wishes,
Miguel

messages.subject: Re: RunLevelData vs ProcessedData objects after normalization: different results
messages.subject_clean: RunLevelData vs ProcessedData objects after normalization: different results
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

currently, the ProcessedData slot of dataProcess() output does not include intensities updated in the imputation step. This is fixed in the development version (github.com/Vitek-Lab/MSstats-dev <http://github.com/Vitek-Lab/MSstats-dev>, develop branch) and will be fixed in the next Bioconductor release. After that update, ProcessedData matches the input to RunlevelData.

Kind regards,
Mateusz

messages.subject: May 3 – May 14, 2021, online: May Institute on computation and statistics for mass spectrometry and proteomics
messages.subject_clean: May 3 – May 14, 2021, online: May Institute on computation and statistics for mass spectrometry and proteomics
messages.body_plain:
Dear Colleagues:

May Institute on Computation and Statistics for Mass Spectrometry and Proteomics, taking place on May 3 – May 14, 2021 on the Boston campus of Northeastern University (online), is now accepting applications.

The program includes tutorials and practical hands-on sessions, presenting open-source data processing tools (Skyline) and statistical analysis tools (R, Bioconductor and MSstats). Instructors are leading experts, who contributed numerous computational methods and software. The presentations are integrated to focus on analyses of several well-chosen datasets. Together we will take an in-depth look into case studies of design and analysis of mass spectrometry-based experiments.

The program also includes keynotes from young investigators, and a "Future developers meeting", that brings together developers (and aspiring developers) of computational tools for mass spectrometry and proteomics. Presentations in the meeting will be selected from the participants' abstracts. We invite you to submit an abstract and present your research.

Week 1:
* Keynote, Brian Searle: Introduction to DIA
* Tutorial, Lindsay Pino: Introduction to DIA proteomics with Skyline
* Hands-on, Brendan MacLean: Part 1:  Skyline processing of proteome-wide DIA of a controlled mixture
* Hands-on, Brendan MacLean: Part 2: Skyline-based comparison of refined versus proteome-wide queries of DIA experiments
* Keynote, Lindsay Pino: Beyond abundance: dynamic quantitative proteomics using Skyline
* Keynote, Isabell Bludau: Expanding the scope of DIA analyses to protein complexes and proteoforms
* Hands-on, Ryan Benz: Part 1: Introduction to R for beginners
* Hands-on, Ryan Benz: Part 2: Introduction to R for beginners

Week 2:
* Tutorial, Kylie Bemis: Intermediate R crash course for MS practitioners
* Tutorial, Olga Vitek: Introduction to statistical methods and MSstats
* Hands-on, Meena Choi and Brendan MacLean: Analysis of data in Skyline Part 1 and Part 2 in MSstats, and comparison of the results
* Tutorial, Mateusz Staniak and Olga Vitek: Introduction to MSstats ecosystem and MSstatsTMT
* Hands-on, Ting Huang and Mateusz Staniak: Use cases of MSstatsTMT
* Keynote. Laurent Gatto: Reproducible MS-based research
* Tutorial, Nuno Bandeira and Meena Choi. Reproducible reporting and reanalysis of quantitative experiments with MassIVE.quant
* Future developers meeting: contributed talks

More information is at https://computationalproteomics.khoury.northeastern.edu/

Please share this widely.

---
Olga Vitek
Professor
Khoury College of Computer Sciences, Northeastern University
URL: olga-vitek-lab.ccis.northeastern.edu <http://olga-vitek-lab.ccis.northeastern.edu>
Twitter: @olgavitek
